prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on your needs (seriousness of injuries, willingness to go to trial, budget, language, etc.). I can’t name a single definitive “best” lawyer, but I can help you find the right one. To get you started quickly:

1) Quick questions so I can narrow recommendations
- What part of Houston (zip code or neighborhood)?  
- How serious are the injuries (minor, hospitalization, permanent disability, wrongful death)?  
- Do you already have an at-fault driver identified and an insurance claim open?  
- Do you need Spanish or another language?  
Answering these lets me tailor a short list.

2) How to find the best personal injury/car-accident lawyer for your situation
- Look for attorneys who focus on car wreck/personal injury (not general practice).  
- Check track record: verdicts/settlements and trial experience for cases like yours. Trial experience matters if the insurer won’t offer fair money.  
- Read recent client reviews (Google, Yelp) and peer ratings (AVVO, Martindale‑Hubbell, Super Lawyers).  
- Confirm license and disciplinary record with the State Bar of Texas (www.texasbar.com).  
- Prefer firms that offer a free initial consultation and work on contingency (no recovery = no fee).

3) Questions to ask at the free consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident cases? How many last year?  
- What percentage of your work is car-accident PI?  
- Do you negotiate or try cases? What’s your trial win rate?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?  
- What is your fee (contingency percentage) and what expenses might I owe?  
- How do you communicate (phone/email) and how often?  
- Can you give references from past clients?

4) Typical fee structure and costs (what to expect)
- Most PI attorneys work on contingency (typical ranges: ~33% if settled before suit; ~36–40% if suit filed; may vary). Confirm the exact percentage and who pays costs if no recovery.  
- You may be responsible for costs advanced for medical records, expert fees, depositions if you lose — get this in writing.

5) Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount or outcome.  
- Requests for large upfront retainer fees.  
- No written fee agreement or unwillingness to put terms in writing.  
- Poor responsiveness during the initial contact.

6) Practical next steps and what to bring to the consult
- Bring police report, photos, medical records/bills, insurance correspondence, witness info, and any accident-related letters.  
- Get at least 2–3 consultations and compare answers, fees, and how comfortable you feel with the lawyer.

7) Want me to find candidates?
If you want, tell me your Houston zip code and the basic facts of the crash and injuries and I’ll produce a short vetted list of well-reviewed personal injury attorneys and a ready-made Google search query and call script you can use.

Would you like me to find a short list for your neighborhood in Houston?
